name: Husam al-Din al-Hajiri
bio: Isa ibn Sanjar ibn Bahram was a poet and soldier from a military family in Erbil. He so often named Hajir, a place in the Hijaz, in his verse that readers came to call him al-Hajiri. His friend Ibn Khallikan heard him recite his poetry, including quatrains, and records his imprisonment first at a fortress outside Erbil and then in the city itself. He died of a knife wound in Erbil in 632 AH (1235 CE).
